**Paris Get‑away: 7‑Day Itinerary (Mid‑Season, €1,200–€1,500 per person)** | Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | |-----|---------|-----------|---------| | **1 – Arrival & Orientation** | • Arrive at Charles de Gaulle (or Orly). Take the RER B or a taxi to your hotel in the 7th arrondissement (near Eiffel Tower).
• Check‑in, freshen up. | • Light stroll along the Seine, visit the **Pont Alexandre III** and **Trocadéro Gardens** for iconic views of the Eiffel Tower. | • Dinner at **Le Jules Verne** (Michelin‑starred, 2‑hour reservation) or a cozy bistro like **Café Constant**. | | **2 – Classic Landmarks** | • Early breakfast at **Café de Flore** (Saint‑Germain‑des‑Près).
• Visit the **Louvre Museum** (arrive before 10 am to avoid crowds). | • Lunch at **Le Café Marly** overlooking the Louvre’s courtyard.
• Walk to **Musée d’Orsay** (impressionist masterpieces). | • Sunset cruise on the Seine (Bateaux Mouches) – 1.5 h, includes dinner. | | **3 – Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur** | • Breakfast at **La Maison Rose**.
• Explore **Montmartre**: Place du Tertre, artists’ square. | • Climb to **Sacré‑Coeur**; panoramic city view.
• Visit **Espace Dalí** or **Moulin Rouge** (optional show). | • Dinner at **Le Coq Rico** (french poultry) or **Le Relais de l’Entrecôte** (steak). | | **4 – Day Trip to Versailles** | • Early train to Versailles (RER C).
• Tour the **Palace of Versailles** (guided audio tour). | • Picnic lunch in the **Gardens of Versailles** (pre‑ordered from **La Petite Venise**).
• Explore the **Grand Trianon** and **Queen’s Hamlet**. | • Return to Paris; light dinner at **L’Atelier de Joël Robuchon** (budget‑friendly). | | **5 – Modern Art & Shopping** | • Breakfast at **Du Pain et des Idées** (croissants).
• Visit **Centre Pompidou** (modern art). | • Lunch at **Le Georges** (museum rooftop).
• Shopping on **Rue Saint‑Honoré** (high‑end boutiques) or **Le Marais** (designer shops). | • Dinner at **Septime** (reservation required) or **Frenchie** (if available). | | **6 – Leisure & Culture** | • Brunch at **Café Charlot** (classic Parisian vibe).
• Visit **Luxembourg Gardens** (relax, maybe a picnic). | • Explore **Panthéon** or **Sorbonne University**.
• Optional: **Père Lachaise Cemetery** (visit Jim Morrison, Oscar Wilde). | • Attend a performance at **Opéra Garnier** (opera or ballet). | | **7 – Departure** | • Pack, last‑minute souvenir shopping at **Marché aux Puces de Saint‑Ouen** (if time). | • Quick lunch at **L’As du Fallafel** (Marais). | • Head to the airport; depart. | --- ### Budget Breakdown (per person) | Category | Approx. Cost (€) | |----------|------------------| | Flights (round‑trip, economy) | 350 | | Accommodation (7 nights, 3‑star hotel) | 400 | | Meals (average €35/day) | 245 | | Transportation (metro + RER + taxis) | 80 | | Attractions & tours (tickets, cruise) | 150 | | Miscellaneous (souvenirs, tips) | 75 | | **Total** | **1,300** | *(Prices are estimates; adjust based on travel dates, hotel choice, and dining preferences.)* --- ### Tips & Recommendations 1. **Book tickets in advance** for the Louvre, Musée d’Orsay, and Versailles to skip long lines. 2. **Use the Paris Visite pass** (valid for 2–5 days) for unlimited metro, bus, and RER within zones 1–3. 3. **Reserve restaurants** at least 2–3 weeks ahead, especially for Michelin‑starred spots. 4. **Carry a reusable water bottle**; many cafés offer free refills. 5. **Pack comfortable shoes**—Paris streets are best explored on foot. 6. **Learn basic French phrases**; locals appreciate the effort. 7. **Check local events** (e.g., Bastille Day celebrations, art fairs) that might affect opening hours. Enjoy your Paris adventure! If you’d like a more tailored plan (e.g., budget, luxury, family‑friendly), just let me know.
